Everything not listed under "change" below I checked and it is as computed.
  > 
  > **Confirmed against the result files** (`primary.csv`, `ratio_by_n`, `bias_bands`, `per_bench`, `highR_vs_main`, `msrc`, `kmstrong`, `ceiling*`, `selected*`, `twopct/`, `extra_*`, `pairwise_bands`, `public_baselines`, `dsweep`): the Results text numbers for the primary endpoint and its intervals (IRT model 0.55/0.65 at n = 10/25, 0.78 at n = 100, 1.96 [1.82, 2.04], about 3.83 at n = 400; kNN 1.12/2.42; ridge 0.73 and 0.88; anchors 0.95/1.03/1.83; CAT 0.68/0.67/1.04; stratified 0.81/0.85/0.83); the leave-one-benchmark-out and versus-stratified numbers (0.91 [0.89, 0.93], 1.00, 1.03, 1.20, 1.23, 0.95, 1.17, 1.23); the bias bands (5.1/6.3/9.7 and 4.9/7.4/12.4 points; difference estimator 0.8/2.0/3.2; sample-mean designs within 0.7); Table 3 (0.27, 4.56, 4.29, 0.42, 0.69); the 100-draw change (max 0.137); the weak prior (1.96 → 1.66, 4.29 → 3.04); the tuned-λ and larger-gap numbers; the suite split, the 2% block (0.63–0.73, 0.88–0.99), the source-count numbers (1.10/1.04, 0.80/0.86), the ceiling numbers (0.93/0.94/1.05 and 0.81/0.82/0.85 against 0.70/0.73/0.85; 0.97 against 0.90 at top 50%); the k-means shift (at most 0.098); Table 11 and the appendix numbers on the published code and the IRT-setting check (all of Table 11 equals `public_baselines.csv` and `dsweep.csv`: stage A 2.49/1.14/1.51/1.38/1.91/1.07, stage B 0.94/0.82/1.05/0.69/0.88/0.69, our 1.99/1.09/2.10/0.79; settings 2.10/1.94/1.99/2.01, 1.60/2.00/1.47/2.04, 2.22/3.38, 1.98/3.04; five of six per-benchmark p-IRT ratios below 1, our plug-in above 1 on all six); the abstract's 0.65–0.79 and 0.80–0.94; the 104 methods and 7 designs; 38 main jobs and 1.4/1.2/0.7 hours, 1.4 hours of sensitivity runs, 4.7 in all, 0.5 to 21.6 minutes per job.
  > 
  > **Confirmed against the code** (`src/bpred/core.py`, `scripts/02_run.py`): Hájek mean; model, plug-in and difference estimators and the five λ; calreg (least squares across sources, evaluated at the sample score, clipped); 5-fold cross-fitting of the sample; stratified, PPS (ε floor, systematic sampling in difficulty order), balanced (greedy from a random pool of 4n), anchor (k-means with k = n, medoid, cluster-size weight), information-top (‖a‖² times the mean of p(1−p) over source abilities), CAT (d = 1 2PL, maximum information at the current MAP); IRT d = 2, N(0, I) prior on ability, MAP target ability, item parameters not refitted; kNN by agreement; kernel ridge; draws (10 per fold and n, 40 in extrapolation; anchor 5 and 10; infotop deterministic; CAT once per target); inner splits (random fifth, family fold, top 25% of the sources); n ≤ N/2; thin = fewer than 10 targets or 5 families; data sizes (79–427 models, 437–12,032 items); the pinned data commit.
  > 
  > **Change (the paper says something the code does not compute):**
  > 1. `results.tex`, ordering paragraph: "pairs one to two points apart are ordered with accuracy 0.55–0.63 by every method and gaps of four to eight points with about 0.89". In `pairwise_bands.csv` (extrapolation, 1–2 points) the range over all methods is 0.53–0.63 (CAT × kNN model 0.53), and 0.89 for 4–8 points holds only for the sample-mean and difference-corrected methods on shared designs (balanced 0.89; uniform, stratified, calreg 0.87–0.88). The model-based predictors and the anchor plug-in are at 0.69 there (uniform × IRT model 0.55 and 0.69; anchor × IRT plug-in 0.57 and 0.69). Say "by the sample-mean and difference-corrected methods" or give the range.
  > 2. `public.tex`: "on our folds, targets and subset-selection seeds". The folds and targets are ours; the published anchors use the k-means / k-medoids random states 0 to 9, not the seeds of our own anchor draws (`scripts/12_public_baselines.py`). The docstring of the script had the same wording; I corrected it (code/ at 4c81743 in `dev`).
  > 3. `reproducibility.
  > [cut here; 6799 characters in Forgejo]
- pull_request_review_rejected reviewed in `paper-repo`#13 ("Candidate 2: paper with recalibration results, published-code comparison and narrowed IRT claims") by `experiment-repo`  > Review of code/ and of the paper's account of it (analysis role). code/ is the anonymised build of my repository (now at 4c81743 in `dev`); the tree contains no internal names, local paths or launch scripts. The results text, the method section and the appendix on the published code agree with the code and the result files except for the six items in experiment-repo#7 (comment 222): (1) the pairwise-accuracy sentence says "every method" and "about 0.89" where the model-based predictors and the anchor plug-in are at 0.69 and the range at 1–2 points is 0.53–0.63; (2) "our subset-selection seeds" in the published-code appendix is wrong (k-means random states 0–9); (3) "CPU-hours" are wall-clock hours; (4) MATH Lvl 5 fall-back is 37–50% by design, not 48%; (5) "do not bring our IRT plug-in below 1.9" holds for the anchor design only; (6) the top-50% best difference cell is 0.95. Also add the fit settings, grids, inner draws, light k-means and the clipping to an appendix paragraph (values in the comment). Requesting changes until 1–4 and the k-means definition are corrected; the rest can go with them.
